A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SE-Agent work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original SWE-bench Verified results, including model comparisons, component ablations, sensitivity analyses and bug-fixing case studies.

after.justification: v6 retains the original experimental results in Table 1, the performance figures and the case studies.

M1.justification: The revision, recombination and refinement operations, reward components and trajectory-selection procedure remain substantively unchanged. The appendix prompts retain the same instructions; notation cleanup and rewritten explanations do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate functional bug repair on the same 500-issue SWE-bench Verified benchmark. The Astropy, scikit-learn and Sphinx case studies are retained, with no added dataset, task or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SWE-Agent and SWE-Search. Both front-page charts also contain the same comparator configurations, including Augment Agent v1, OpenHands, Moatless Tools, Tools, Refact.ai Agent and TRAE. Changes to model-name hyphenation do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The benchmark, Pass@1/Pass@5 metrics, five-model comparison, default trajectory count and sensitivity-test settings are retained. The new Claude-4-Sonnet footnote describes the configuration behind an 80.0% result already plotted in v1; it does not establish a changed experiment or protocol.

E4.justification: The three component ablations, resolved-issue overlap analysis, trajectory-count and API-cost analyses, and case studies are unchanged. v1 Figures 5, 6 and 7 correspond to v6 Figures 6, 7 and 5, respectively; their relocation adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The existing Pass@1/Pass@5 reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All Table 1 scores match, and the ablation, sensitivity and overlap results are retained. Both front-page charts already report SE-Agent at 80.0% and SWE-Agent with Claude-4-Sonnet at 66.6%. The percentages added to v6's abstract restate existing results.

T1.justification: The environment, trajectory, objective, reward and selection formulations retain the same mathematical meaning. v6 standardizes symbols, fixes indexing and weight-label inconsistencies, and numbers equations, without adding substantive assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about trajectory-level self-evolution, solution diversity, improvements across LLMs and state-of-the-art open-source-agent performance remain the same. Adding existing performance percentages to the abstract does not expand these claims' scientific scope.

C2.justification: The explanations involving cross-trajectory insights, escaping local optima, revision-enabled diversity and trajectory evolution as an implicit regularizer are retained. Trimming the future-work examples does not establish a changed applicability boundary, and no substantive limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: A new footnote identifies Claude-4-Sonnet and the SWE-Agent configuration associated with the existing 80.0% result. The code-access pointer changes from wanghuacan/SE-Agent to JARVIS-Xs/SE-Agent. Planning counts, hardware and API details move from v1 Appendix A to v6 Section 5.1 rather than being newly disclosed.

R1.justification: The same 45 works remain cited, with the same positioning relative to code agents, MCTS, ReAct enhancements, evolutionary computation and self-play. Author-list and access-date edits are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The preliminary, method and experimental sections receive sustained prose revision and terminology cleanup. Trajectory notation is standardized throughout, implementation details move into the experimental setup, the prompt appendix is reorganized, and the case-study narrative and conclusion are repositioned. This substantially revises exposition while preserving the science.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, plots are enlarged and restyled, and Table 1 gains expanded framework headers. Case-study figures are reordered and grouped before the conclusion instead of appearing partly among references. Appendix prompt boxes are recolored and extensively reflowed, producing a substantial visual and layout revision.

improvement.justification: v6 improves interpretability by explaining the configuration behind the previously unexplained 80.0% result, standardizing notation, correcting case-study references and placing implementation details beside the experimental setup. These are useful clarity and navigation gains. The brief new footnote still provides limited reproducibility information for that result, and the empirical evidence remains unchanged.
